events.label: birth
events.text: Born Carl Friedrich Heinrich Reinhard Scheer.

evidence.quote: Carl Friedrich Heinrich Reinhard Scheer ( 30 September 1863

events.text: Entered the Imperial German Navy as a cadet, aged 15.

evidence.quote: Reinhard Scheer entered the navy on 22 April 1879 aged 15 as a cadet

events.text: Began first training cruise aboard Niobe, June to September 1879.

evidence.quote: His first cruise aboard Niobe lasted from June to September 1879

events.text: Assigned to the Naval School in Kiel for officer training.

evidence.quote: Following his return to Germany in September , Scheer was assigned to the Naval School in Kiel

events.text: Transferred to East Africa Squadron; first tour began.

evidence.quote: his first tour with the unit lasted from 1884 to 1886

events.label: military_action
events.text: Took part in a landing party that suppressed a chieftain in Kamerun.

evidence.quote: in December 1884 , Scheer participated in a landing party that suppressed a pro-British indigenous chieftain in Kamerun

events.text: Returned to Germany, ending first East Africa Squadron tour.

evidence.quote: his first tour with the unit lasted from 1884 to 1886
After his return to Germany in 1886

events.text: Torpedo training aboard a ship, January to May 1888.

events.text: Rejoined East Africa Squadron as torpedo officer aboard a corvette.

evidence.quote: In May 1888 , Scheer returned to the East Africa Squadron as a torpedo officer aboard the corvette

events.text: East Africa Squadron tour ended in early summer 1890.

evidence.quote: This tour lasted until early summer 1890

events.text: Made instructor at the Torpedo Research Command in Kiel.

evidence.quote: at which point Scheer returned to Germany , where he was made an instructor at the Torpedo Research Command

events.text: Transferred by Tirpitz to Reichsmarineamt Torpedo Section.

evidence.quote: In 1897 , following Tirpitzs promotion to Secretary of State of the Imperial Navy Office , he transferred Scheer to the Reichsmarineamt

events.text: Promoted to Kapitän zur See.

evidence.quote: Scheer was promoted to Kapitän zur See in 1905

events.text: Took command of a battleship, held for two years.

evidence.quote: took command of the battleship in 1907

events.text: Battleship command ended after two years.

evidence.quote: took command of the battleship in 1907 , a command he held for two years

events.text: Report recommended him for promotion.

evidence.quote: A report dated 1 December 1909 recommended Scheer for promotion

events.text: Ended term as chief of staff to Admiral Holtzendorff.

evidence.quote: He held the Chief of Staff position until late 1911

events.text: Transferred back to the Reichsmarineamt under Tirpitz.

evidence.quote: He held the Chief of Staff position until late 1911 , when he was transferred back to the RMA under Tirpitz

events.text: Held post of Chief of the General Naval Department through 1912.

evidence.quote: held the position of Chief of the General Naval Department through 1912

events.text: Became squadron commander of the II Battle Squadron, six battleships.

evidence.quote: squadron commander for the six battleships of the II Battle Squadron of the High Seas Fleet in January 1913

events.text: Promoted to Vizeadmiral.

evidence.quote: On 9 December 1913 , Scheer was promoted to Vizeadmiral

events.text: Left command of the II Battle Squadron.

evidence.quote: He remained with the II Battle Squadron until January 1915

events.text: Took command of the III Battle Squadron.

evidence.quote: He thereafter took command of the III Battle Squadron

events.text: Promoted to Admiral.

evidence.quote: In January 1916 , he was promoted to Admiral

events.text: Became Commander in chief of the High Seas Fleet.

evidence.quote: Vice Admiral Scheer became Commander in chief of the High Seas Fleet on 18 January 1916

events.text: Wrote Guiding Principles for Sea Warfare in the North Sea.

evidence.quote: Upon promotion to the position , Scheer wrote Guiding Principles for Sea Warfare in the North Sea

evidence.quote: the Kaiser approved the
memorandum on 23 February 1916 .

evidence.quote: Following the Kaisers order forbidding unrestricted submarine warfare on 24 April 1916 , Scheer ordered all of the U-boats

events.text: Led German High Seas Fleet at Battle of Jutland, 31 May to 1 June.

events.label: operation
events.text: Began raiding British convoys to Norway with light fleet elements.

evidence.quote: In later 1917 , Scheer began to use light elements of the fleet to raid British convoys to Norway

events.text: Unrestricted submarine campaign resumed after Scheer's advocacy.

evidence.quote: Ultimately , Scheer and his allies prevailed and the unrestricted submarine campaign was resumed in February 1917

In August 1918 , Scheer was promoted to the Chief of Naval Staff

Scheer wrote his memoirs of the Great War in 1919

events.text: Wife Emillie murdered by an intruder at their home.

evidence.quote: In October 1920 , an intruder broke into Scheers house and murdered his wife , Emillie

events.label: withdrawal
events.text: Retreated into solitude after the incident.

evidence.quote: Following the incident , Scheer retreated into solitude
